patch.description:
**Deprecated:** this endpoint is moving to cloud-platform at the same path; the cloud-platform base URL will be announced. Behaviour may differ in edge cases.

Upserts (inserts or updates) pricing and metadata for one or more models. Only authenticated admins can perform this operation.
The body should be an array of objects where each key is a model name and the value is the model data.

`providerConfig` on an existing model merges into the stored config at the top level:
keys sent replace stored keys, a key sent as `null` is removed, and omitted keys are kept.
A new model stores `providerConfig` as sent.

`providerConfig.api_key` is returned as `"***"` by admin reads. Sending `"***"` back keeps
the stored key, and is rejected with 400 when no key is stored. Changing `backend` or
`base_url` while keeping a stored key is rejected; send `api_key` again, or `null` to use
the server key, which is only sent to the provider's official HTTPS host.

A `providerConfig` write applies only if the stored config has not changed since it was
read for the merge; otherwise it fails with 409 and can be retried.

Admin permissions: admin session or read_write token. A read_only token receives HTTP 403 with error.type insufficient_permissions before the handler runs.

post.summary: Deprecate a model in favor of another (Admin only)
post.description:
**Deprecated:** this endpoint is moving to cloud-platform at the same path; the cloud-platform base URL will be announced. Behaviour may differ in edge cases.

Atomically marks `modelId` as deprecated and routes its traffic to
`successorModelId`:
1. Adds `modelId` as an alias of `successorModelId`, so existing clients
   sending `model: "<modelId>"` keep working — the alias resolver rewrites
   the request-side `model` field to the successor before backend dispatch,
   and the response's `model` field reflects the canonical (successor) name.
2. Re-points any pre-existing inbound aliases of `modelId` at the
   successor, so historical aliases keep resolving.
3. Sets `modelId.isActive = false` so it is hidden from public
   `GET /v1/models` and from `GET /v1/admin/models` unless
   `include_inactive=true`.
4. Records a `model_history` entry for audit purposes.

All steps run in a single DB transaction. If the successor is inactive or
either model is missing, returns 404 without modifying state.

Admin permissions: admin session or read_write token. A read_only token receives HTTP 403 with error.type insufficient_permissions before the handler runs.

400.description: Invalid request (e.g. self-deprecation, empty model id)

403.description: Missing admin privileges (forbidden) or insufficient token permission (insufficient_permissions).

404.description: Either model not found, or successor is not active

(`tinfoil`, `chutes`). Each section lists the provider's compiled pins and

trust versions and served from memory until one changes.

get.description:
Get hardware attestation report for TEE verification. The API key is
optional, so a client can verify the gateway before it sends any
credential. Without a key, listed models only; with one, also the unlisted
models the key's organization may use. A key that is sent must be valid.
Report retrieval is non-billable — no usage or billing records are created.

With `model=...&provider=chutes`, the Chutes entry in `model_attestations` includes
`quote_b64`, `certificate_b64`, `e2e_pubkey`, `nonce`, and `gpu_evidence` for
the selected verified instance. `gpu_evidence` preserves every GPU's `arch`,
`certificate` (base64 device certificate chain), and `evidence` (base64 SPDM
evidence) from the same evidence request as the CPU quote and certificate.
`gpu_verdict` remains available as verification metadata.

The GPU challenge is `SHA256(UTF8(nonce + e2e_pubkey))`, using the returned
nonce's hex text and public key's base64 text without decoding either input.
Pass the hex-encoded digest as the NVIDIA verification nonce; it is also bound
into the CPU quote's `report_data[0:32]`. The raw client nonce is not the GPU
challenge.

parameters.name: include_tls_fingerprint
parameters.description:
Include the TLS certificate SPKI fingerprint in the report-data binding.
Defaults to false; when true, report_data[..32] = SHA256(signing_address || tls_cert_fingerprint).

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Restrict the report to a specific provider.
Accepted values: `near` (NEAR AI's own TEE fleet), `chutes`, or `tinfoil` (attested third-party sources).
When omitted, the first successfully responding provider is used.

400.description: Invalid nonce, signing_algo or provider, or unknown model (a model the caller may not use is reported as unknown)

401.description: An API key was sent and is invalid

PrivacyClassifyRequestDoc.description:
Privacy classification endpoint (passthrough)

Proxies privacy classification requests to a token-classification model
(e.g. `openai/privacy-filter`) that returns PII spans with categories and scores.
Only the `model` field is read from the request for routing; the rest is forwarded as-is.

These documentation-only types approximate the request and response bodies
for OpenAPI schema generation. The runtime handler still accepts a raw
`Bytes` body and forwards it transparently to the provider.

threshold.description: Optional minimum confidence score for returned spans (0.0–1.0).

id.description: Upstream response ID; use this ID at /v1/signature/{id}.

index.description: Index of this entry into the input list (matches input order).

redacted.description: Input text rewritten with placeholders in place of detected PII.

usage.description: Per-input usage (input_tokens billed for this entry).

PrivacyRedactRequestDoc.description:
Privacy redaction endpoint

Sends each input text through the privacy-filter model and returns it
rewritten with realistic-looking dummies in place of detected PII
(e.g. `redacted1@example.com`, `+1-555-0100`, `Redacted001`). Useful as
a one-shot sanitizer ahead of calling a third-party LLM. The original
PII is **never** echoed back; only the redacted form is returned.

Internally this is a `/v1/privacy/classify` call plus local span-apply
— same billing (one input_tokens charge per input), same concurrency
limits, same model routing.

outside this typed schema. The typed adapter also executes hosted web search

tags.name: Responses
tags.description:
Stateless response inference. Both paths normalize omitted or null `store` to `false` and reject `store: true`. Raw request/response content, response items, and history are not persisted. Clients must include any prior context in each request. Canonical `openai/` models use one upstream native Responses request after alias resolution. Other models use the typed adapter, with bounded request-scoped inference rounds when hosted search is requested.

Both paths accept client-managed `function` and `custom` tools, including tools grouped in a `namespace`, and leading developer `additional_tools` declarations. Cloud returns calls without executing them; clients replay each `function_call` or `custom_tool_call` with its matching output and caller-managed history. Preserve `call_id`, names, namespaces, raw arguments or custom input, and provider metadata such as `thought_signature`. The typed replay path accepts assistant `output_text` parts and plaintext `reasoning` items, using reasoning content or its summary as prior assistant context. Encrypted-only reasoning requires a native Responses backend. The typed adapter supports text custom tools and the Codex `exec` Lark source grammar; other grammars require a native backend.

Each generated item has its own `output_index`. Tool calls finish with `response.output_item.done`; a successful model turn ends with `response.completed`, including when tools await client execution. Reasoning uses `response.reasoning_text.delta`; failures expose `response.error` in `response.failed` and preserve partial usage.

The typed adapter executes `web_search` and `web_context_search` using a bounded request-scoped loop, emits search lifecycle events and URL citations, and accumulates usage across inference rounds without storing history. Optional `web_search.count` (0–20) overrides model-selected counts; 0 skips the search provider. If a model emits client tool calls and searches in the same round, client calls are returned without executing that round's searches. On the typed path, completed search output markers may accompany replayed assistant text, but raw search results are not restored across requests. Native Responses also accepts top-level `web_search`, executed by the upstream provider without a Cloud search loop. Complete native `web_search_call` replay items, search configuration, and `include` are forwarded unchanged; provider-returned search citations and sources retain their native shape. `file_search`, `code_interpreter`, `computer`, and remote `mcp` are unsupported. Image-generation/editing models are rejected on both paths. The separate `POST /mcp` endpoint exposes its `web_search` tool independently of Responses; use `/v1/images/*` for image generation/editing. Existing completed-response gateway attestation is preserved best-effort: when the signature write succeeds, `GET /v1/signature/resp_*` retrieves signatures over SHA-256 request/response digests, never raw content. Interrupted streams create no `resp_*` attestation record or legacy disconnect fallback. Responses rejects conversation linkage, response history, and file input; the separate Conversation and File endpoints are not part of Responses inference.
